title.ja: Bedrock: tool use、構造化出力、Guardrails、prompt caching、inference profile、batch
title.en: Bedrock: Tool Use, Structured Output, Guardrails, Prompt Caching, Inference Profiles, and Batch

sources.title: Use a tool to complete an Amazon Bedrock model response
supports: The model does not call a tool itself: the application (client-side) or Bedrock (server-side) runs it and returns the result
Three modes: client-side tool use (Responses, Chat Completions, Converse, InvokeModel), server-side tool use (currently the Responses API), Anthropic-defined tool types

sources.title: Client-side tool use
supports: With Converse the response has stopReason tool_use and toolUse blocks; the application appends the assistant message and a user message with toolResult blocks, with status error for a failed tool
toolUseId is generated by Bedrock for tools defined in toolConfig (prefix tooluse_), but for some models the provider's identifier is passed through

sources.title: Server-side tool use
supports: Server-side tool calling is available with the Responses API: Bedrock invokes a Lambda function that implements MCP

sources.title: Inference using Converse API
supports: ConverseStream event order: messageStart, per content block contentBlockStart (tool use only), contentBlockDelta (text, reasoning, or tool use partial JSON), contentBlockStop, then messageStop with stopReason, then metadata with usage and metrics
contentBlockIndex correlates the events of one content block
Request fields guardrailConfig, toolConfig, serviceTier, requestMetadata (key-value tags recorded in model invocation logs)
Converse needs bedrock:InvokeModel; ConverseStream needs bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream

sources.title: ConverseStream (API reference)
supports: Request members toolConfig, guardrailConfig (GuardrailStreamConfiguration), outputConfig, requestMetadata, serviceTier

sources.title: MessageStopEvent
supports: stopReason values: end_turn, tool_use, max_tokens, stop_sequence, guardrail_intervened, content_filtered, malformed_model_output, malformed_tool_use, model_context_window_exceeded

sources.title: ToolSpecification, ToolUseBlock, ToolResultBlock, ToolChoice, ContentBlockStart/Delta (API reference)
supports: ToolSpecification: name ([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+, 1-64), description, inputSchema, strict
ToolUseBlockStart carries name and toolUseId; ToolUseBlockDelta carries input as a string
ToolResultBlock.status (success | error) is supported only by Amazon Nova and Anthropic Claude 3 and 4 models
ToolChoice: auto (default), any, tool (a named tool; only Anthropic Claude 3 and Amazon Nova models)
sources.note: Read together with API_runtime_ToolUseBlock, API_runtime_ToolUseBlockStart, API_runtime_ToolUseBlockDelta, API_runtime_ToolResultBlock, API_runtime_ToolChoice, API_runtime_ContentBlockDelta and API_runtime_ContentBlockStart on the same day.

sources.title: Get validated JSON results from models
supports: Two mechanisms: a JSON Schema output format (outputConfig.textFormat for Converse) and strict tool use (strict: true on a tool definition)

Supported subset of JSON Schema Draft 2020-12; not supported: recursive schemas, external $ref, minimum/maximum/multipleOf, minLength/maxLength, additionalProperties other than false; array minItems only 0 and 1
A new schema is compiled on first use, which may take up to a few minutes; compiled grammars are cached for 24 hours
Supported with Converse/ConverseStream, InvokeModel, cross-Region inference, and (according to this page) batch inference; model support is on each model card
Structured outputs are incompatible with citations for Anthropic models
sources.note: This page lists batch inference as supported. The batch inference overview page says batch does not support tool calling or structured output. The two pages disagree; the chapter says so.

sources.title: OutputConfig, OutputFormat, JsonSchemaDefinition (API reference)
supports: outputConfig.textFormat has type json_schema and structure.jsonSchema with schema (a string), name and description
sources.note: Read together with API_runtime_OutputFormat, API_runtime_OutputFormatStructure and API_runtime_JsonSchemaDefinition.

sources.title: Detect and filter harmful content by using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
supports: Filters: content filters (Hate, Insults, Sexual, Violence, Misconduct, Prompt Attack), denied topics, word filters, sensitive information filters, contextual grounding checks, Automated Reasoning checks
A guardrail has a working draft and numbered versions; it is used by passing its ID and version on an inference call, or alone through ApplyGuardrail
Reasoning content blocks are not evaluated

sources.title: Include a guardrail with the Converse API
supports: guardrailConfig carries guardrailIdentifier, guardrailVersion, trace; ConverseStream adds streamProcessingMode
With tools, a guardrail does not evaluate toolResult content, tool definitions, or the toolUse input the model generates; it evaluates text and guardContent

When blocked: stopReason guardrail_intervened, the configured blocked message is returned as the output (in the streamed message for ConverseStream), the trace is in metadata, and the documented example shows zero tokens
Once any guardContent block is present, only guardContent blocks are evaluated; a system prompt is evaluated only inside guardContent

sources.title: Configure streaming response behavior to filter content
supports: Synchronous mode (default) buffers and scans chunks before they are sent, adding latency; asynchronous mode sends chunks immediately and blocks later chunks once a violation is found
Masking of sensitive information is not supported in asynchronous mode

sources.title: GuardrailStreamConfiguration (API reference)
supports: Members guardrailIdentifier, guardrailVersion (a number or DRAFT), streamProcessingMode (sync | async), trace (enabled | disabled | enabled_full)

sources.title: Set up permissions to use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
supports: A role that invokes a model with a guardrail needs bedrock:ApplyGuardrail on arn:aws:bedrock:<region>:<account>:guardrail/<id> in addition to the InvokeModel permissions

sources.title: Supported Regions and models for Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
supports: Guardrails apply to InvokeModel, InvokeModelWithResponseStream, Converse and ConverseStream on bedrock-runtime; the bedrock-mantle endpoint does not support them
The page lists the models that do not support guardrails (embedding, rerank, speech and some others); Nova 2 Lite and Claude Haiku 4.5 are not on that list

sources.title: Safeguard tiers for guardrails policies
supports: Tiers apply to content filters (including prompt attacks) and denied topics
Classic tier supports English, French and Spanish; Standard tier has broader language support, prompt leakage detection, and uses cross-Region inference
Safeguard tiers are available in Asia Pacific (Tokyo) among other Regions

sources.title: Languages supported by Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
supports: Japanese is 'Optimized and supported' for content filters and prompt attacks and for denied topics in the Standard tier, and for sensitive information filters
Classic tier content filters and denied topics, word filters, and contextual grounding checks list English, French and Spanish only
Guardrails are ineffective with languages that are not supported

sources.title: Supported Regions for cross-Region guardrail inference
supports: Guardrail profile apac.guardrail.v1:0: from source ap-northeast-1 the destinations are ap-south-1, ap-northeast-3, ap-northeast-2, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2 and ap-northeast-1
sources.note: Read with guardrails-cross-region.html (prompts and results may move outside the primary Region; the configuration stays in the primary Region) and guardrail-profiles-permissions.html (bedrock:ApplyGuardrail on the guardrail and on the guardrail profile in each destination Region).

sources.title: Remove PII from conversations by using sensitive information filters
supports: Block or mask (anonymize) modes; built-in entity types include EMAIL, PHONE, AWS_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_SECRET_KEY; custom regex patterns
The filter does not evaluate toolUse input, toolResult content, or tool definitions

sources.title: Detect prompt attacks with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
supports: Prompt attack types: jailbreaks, prompt injection, and prompt leakage (Standard tier only); the filter is a content filter of type PROMPT_ATTACK configured with inputStrength

sources.title: Prompt injection security
supports: Preventing prompt injection is the customer's responsibility under the shared responsibility model, compared to SQL injection; guardrails are offered as a help, not a guarantee

sources.title: Prompt caching for faster model inference
supports: Implicit caching is best effort; explicit caching uses cache checkpoints, with a per-model minimum prefix (512 to 4,096 tokens) counted cumulatively across tools, system and messages

Nova 2 Lite: minimum 1K tokens, 4 checkpoints, 5-minute TTL, checkpoints in system and messages, at most 20K cached tokens. Claude Haiku 4.5: 4,096 tokens, 4 checkpoints, 5 minutes or 1 hour, system, messages and tools
The TTL resets on each cache hit; a checkpoint in front of too few tokens still succeeds but is not cached; a ttl field on a model that supports only 5 minutes can cause a ValidationException
Usage reports cacheReadInputTokens and cacheWriteInputTokens; inputTokens then counts only non-cached input; total input = inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheWriteInputTokens
Checkpoints are processed in the order tools, system, messages; prompt caching is not supported with batch inference

sources.title: TokenUsage and CachePointBlock (API reference)
supports: TokenUsage: inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens, cacheReadInputTokens, cacheWriteInputTokens, cacheDetails
CachePointBlock: type default, optional ttl 5m | 1h

sources.title: Set up a model invocation resource using inference profiles
supports: System-defined cross-Region profiles and application inference profiles (user-created, taggable for cost tracking, over one model or one cross-Region profile)
The price of an inference profile is that of the model in the Region the profile is called from

sources.title: Prerequisites for inference profiles
supports: A policy that names an inference profile must also name the foundation model in each Region of the profile; bedrock:InferenceProfileArn restricts model access to calls through one profile
A global profile needs the Region-less model ARN; aws:RequestedRegion equal to 'unspecified' can be denied to block global routing

sources.title: Route model inference requests across AWS Regions with cross-Region inference
supports: Geographic profiles keep processing within a geography; global profiles may use any supported commercial Region and cost about 10% less
Data in transit stays on the AWS network and is encrypted; CloudTrail logs the request in the source Region with additionalEventData.inferenceRegion
Inference profiles do not support Provisioned Throughput

sources.title: Model card: Nova 2 Lite
supports: bedrock-runtime features supported: response streaming, guardrails, client-side tool calling; not supported: structured outputs, count tokens, knowledge base, agents, prompt management, intelligent prompt routing
Tokyo: no In-Region access, Geo (jp. profile to ap-northeast-1 and ap-northeast-3) and Global
Lifecycle Active; EOL no sooner than Dec 02, 2026; legacy period at least 6 months
Service tiers: Standard, Priority and Flex yes; Reserved no
Explicit prompt caching: 1K minimum, 4 checkpoints, 5 minutes, system and messages

sources.title: Model card: Claude Haiku 4.5
supports: bedrock-runtime features supported include guardrails, count tokens, structured outputs and client-side tool calling; structured outputs are not supported through the India geographic profile
bedrock-runtime requires a geo or global inference profile; jp. profile routes to ap-northeast-1 and ap-northeast-3
Lifecycle Active; EOL no sooner than Oct 16, 2026; legacy period at least 6 months
Explicit prompt caching: 4,096 minimum, 4 checkpoints, 5 minutes and 1 hour, system, messages and tools

sources.title: Model lifecycle
supports: States Active, Legacy, End-of-Life; visible as modelLifecycle in GetFoundationModel and ListFoundationModels
Once Legacy begins new customers cannot adopt the model and existing customers may lose access after 15 days of inactivity; after EOL requests fail; migration is not automatic
sources.note: Models launched before September 7, 2026 follow model-lifecycle-legacy.html (at least 12 months on Bedrock before EOL, at least 6 months in Legacy), which was read on the same day.

sources.title: Quotas for Amazon Bedrock
supports: Inference is controlled by quotas on token usage; the values applied to an account may be lower than the published defaults; increases are not automatic
bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle have separate per-model quotas

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock endpoints and quotas (AWS General Reference)
supports: Published defaults: cross-Region requests per minute 2,000 (Nova 2 Lite, not adjustable) and 10,000 (Claude Haiku 4.5); cross-Region tokens per minute 8,000,000 (Nova 2 Lite) and 5,000,000 (Claude Haiku 4.5)
Batch inference: minimum 100 records per job, 100,000 records per job and per input file, input file size 1 GB, for both Nova 2 Lite and Claude Haiku 4.5; job size 5 GB for Claude Haiku 4.5

sources.title: How tokens are counted in Amazon Bedrock
supports: At the start of a request, total input tokens plus max_tokens is deducted from the tokens-per-minute quota; at the end the deduction becomes InputTokenCount + CacheWriteInputTokenCount + OutputTokenCount x burndown rate
Burndown rate for output tokens: 5x for Anthropic models version 4.7 and below, 1x for models not listed; cache reads do not count toward the quota

sources.title: Service tiers for optimizing performance and cost
supports: Reserved, Priority, Standard and Flex tiers; Flex trades longer processing times for a discount; the on-demand quota is shared across Priority, Standard and Flex

sources.title: Troubleshooting Amazon Bedrock API Error Codes
supports: 429 ThrottlingException means an account quota was exceeded; 503 ServiceUnavailable and model-not-ready errors are capacity, not quota

sources.title: Monitor your token usage by counting tokens before running inference
supports: CountTokens returns the input token count without charge; support is per model (model card)

sources.title: Process multiple prompts with batch inference
supports: Input in InvokeModel or Converse format; results are written to S3; not supported for provisioned models
Batch inference does not support tool calling or structured output

sources.title: Format and upload your batch inference data
supports: Each line of a .jsonl file is { recordId, modelInput }; with the Converse invocation type modelInput is a Converse request body; output order is not guaranteed
sources.note: Read with batch-inference-results.html (output lines carry modelOutput or an error object; manifest.json.out has record and token counts), batch-inference-supported.html (Nova 2 Lite and Claude Haiku 4.5: cross-Region profile support including ap-northeast-1, no single-Region support), batch-inference-create.html (modelInvocationType InvokeModel | Converse) and batch-iam-sr.html (service role trust and permissions).

sources.title: Increase model invocation capacity with Provisioned Throughput
supports: Billed hourly per model unit, with no commitment, 1 month or 6 months; billing continues until it is deleted; required for customized models

sources.title: Automate tasks in your application using AI agents
supports: Amazon Bedrock Agents is now Agents Classic and is no longer open to new customers (from July 30, 2026); AgentCore is the recommended path

sources.title: What is Amazon Bedrock AgentCore?
supports: AgentCore is a set of services: Harness (a managed agent loop in an isolated microVM per session), Runtime, Memory, Gateway (APIs and Lambda functions as MCP tools), Identity, Code Interpreter, Browser, Observability, Payments, Evaluations

sources.title: Monitor model invocation using CloudWatch Logs and Amazon S3
supports: Model invocation logging is off by default; when on it stores full request and response data for Converse, ConverseStream, InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream in CloudWatch Logs or S3

sources.title: Invoking Lambda function URLs
supports: With AuthType AWS_IAM the event's requestContext.authorizer.iam carries accessKey, accountId, callerId, userArn and userId

sources.title: AWS::Bedrock::Guardrail and AWS::Bedrock::GuardrailVersion (CloudFormation)
supports: Properties BlockedInputMessaging, BlockedOutputsMessaging, ContentPolicyConfig, CrossRegionConfig, SensitiveInformationPolicyConfig, Name; GuardrailVersion takes GuardrailIdentifier and returns Version

sources.title: Resource types that support Cloud Control API
supports: AWS::Bedrock::Guardrail and AWS::Bedrock::GuardrailVersion are listed

sources.title: @go-to-k/cdkd 0.296.28 (installed package)
supports: The distributed code registers SDK providers for AWS::IAM::Role, AWS::IAM::Policy, AWS::Lambda::Function, AWS::Lambda::Url, AWS::DynamoDB::Table and AWS::Logs::LogGroup
No provider is registered for AWS::Bedrock::Guardrail or AWS::Bedrock::GuardrailVersion and neither is in its NON_PROVISIONABLE list, so both go through the Cloud Control fallback
sources.note: Read in node_modules/@go-to-k/cdkd/dist (program-*.js and deploy-engine-*.js), not on GitHub.

sources.title: @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime 3.1149.0 (installed package)
supports: The pinned types declare outputConfig, ToolSpecification.strict, CachePointBlock.ttl, GuardrailStreamConfiguration.streamProcessingMode, requestMetadata and cacheReadInputTokens

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock pricing
supports: Batch inference is offered at 50% of on-demand price for select models; Flex tier is a 50% discount to Standard

Guardrails: content filters and denied topics USD 0.15 per 1,000 text units each, sensitive information filters USD 0.10, regular-expression sensitive filters and word filters free; pricing is the same for both tiers
A text unit is up to 1,000 characters; longer text is charged as several units

sources.title: AWS Price List: Amazon Bedrock, ap-northeast-1
supports: Nova 2 Lite in Tokyo: cache read USD 0.000099 and cache write USD 0 per 1K tokens; batch and flex input USD 0.000198 and output USD 0.0016555 per 1K tokens
Guardrail text units in Tokyo: sensitive information USD 0.0001 and content policy USD 0.00015 per text unit

sources.title: AWS Price List: Bedrock models sold through AWS Marketplace, ap-northeast-1
supports: Claude Haiku 4.5 regional: cache read USD 0.11, 5-minute cache write USD 1.375, 1-hour cache write USD 2.20, batch input USD 0.55 and batch output USD 2.75 per million tokens

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers AI: Function calling
supports: Workers AI offers traditional function calling and embedded function calling (runWithTools from @cloudflare/ai-utils runs the function code alongside the inference call)

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers AI: JSON Mode
supports: response_format with type json_object or json_schema, compatible with OpenAI's form, on the models the page lists

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers AI: Asynchronous Batch API
supports: A batch of requests is queued and answered later, polled by request_id; the total payload must be under 10 MB

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers AI: Prompt caching
supports: Prefix caching is on by default for select models, cached input tokens are billed at a discount, and the x-session-affinity header routes a session to the instance that holds the cache

sources.title: Cloudflare AI Gateway
supports: A proxy in front of model providers with analytics, logging, caching of identical requests, rate limiting, retries and fallback; core features are free
Amazon Bedrock is a supported provider: the gateway can sign requests with stored AWS credentials (BYOK)
sources.note: Read with ai-gateway/features/caching/, ai-gateway/features/rate-limiting/, ai-gateway/reference/pricing/ and ai-gateway/usage/providers/bedrock/.

sources.title: Cloudflare AI Gateway: Guardrails usage considerations
supports: Guardrails run Llama Guard 3 8B on Workers AI and incur Workers AI usage; listed languages do not include Japanese
Streaming requests are not enforced as streams: the gateway endpoint buffers the whole response and returns it unstreamed

sources.title: Cloudflare Agents
supports: Agents run on a durable runtime (identity, SQL storage, scheduling) with a harness that defines the loop, or a loop you build on the Agents SDK

sources.title: Vercel AI Gateway
supports: One endpoint for models of many providers, with centralized credentials, request logs, spend budgets, routing and provider failover, usable from any infrastructure

sources.title: Vercel AI Gateway: Pricing
supports: No markup and no platform fee on tokens on the paid tier, including with your own provider key; free-tier requests are rate limited per model

sources.title: AI SDK: Tool calling
supports: A tool has an inputSchema used both to tell the model and to validate its call; stopWhen with isStepCount(n) bounds the multi-step loop that generateText and streamText run

sources.title: AI SDK: Generating structured data
supports: Output.object({ schema }) generates and validates structured data against a Zod, Valibot or JSON schema

sources.title: AI SDK: Amazon Bedrock provider
supports: The Bedrock provider passes guardrailConfig through provider options and supports guardContent on message parts

definition.ja: モデルが、アプリの用意した関数を名前と入力で指定して実行を求めること。実行するのはアプリで、モデルではない。
definition.en: A model asking for one of the application's functions by name and input. The application runs it, not the model.

definition.ja: tool use に対してアプリが返す結果。次のリクエストの user メッセージに入れてモデルへ渡す。
definition.en: What the application returns for a tool use, sent to the model in the next request's user message.

definition.ja: モデルの出力を、指定した JSON Schema に合う JSON に限る機能。合った JSON でも、業務上の条件はアプリが検証する。
definition.en: Constraining a model's output to JSON that fits a given JSON Schema. The application still validates what the schema cannot say.

definition.ja: Bedrock Guardrails の設定の単位。入力と出力のテキストを決めたフィルターで調べ、該当すれば決めたメッセージに差し替える。
definition.en: A unit of configuration in Bedrock Guardrails. It checks input and output text with the filters you chose and replaces it with a set message on a match.

definition.ja: Guardrails の課金単位。1,000 文字までが 1 unit。
definition.en: The billing unit of Guardrails: up to 1,000 characters is one unit.

definition.ja: 毎回同じ内容で始まるプロンプトの先頭部分を、モデルの側で使い回す機能。読み出した分は入力より安い単価で課金される。
definition.en: Reusing, on the model's side, the part of a prompt that starts the same way every time. Tokens read from the cache are billed below the input rate.

definition.ja: プロンプトの中で、ここまでをキャッシュの対象にすると示す目印。Converse API では cachePoint ブロック。
definition.en: A mark in a prompt that says everything up to here may be cached. In the Converse API it is a cachePoint block.

definition.ja: 多数のリクエストを S3 のファイルで渡し、結果をあとで S3 に受け取る推論。すぐには返らない代わりに安い。
definition.en: Inference where many requests are handed over as a file in S3 and the results arrive in S3 later, cheaper because it is not immediate.

definition.ja: 出力 1 トークンが、分あたりのトークンのクォータを何トークン分減らすかの倍率。モデルごとに違う。
definition.en: How many tokens of the tokens-per-minute quota one output token uses up. It differs by model.

definition.ja: モデルの処理能力を時間課金で確保する買い方。消すまで課金が続く。
definition.en: Buying a model's capacity by the hour. It is billed until you delete it.

glossary.ja: プロンプトインジェクション

definition.ja: モデルが読むデータの中に指示を書き、開発者の指示の代わりに従わせようとする攻撃。
definition.en: An attack that writes instructions into data a model reads, to have them followed in place of the developer's.

glossary.ja: モデルのライフサイクル

definition.ja: Bedrock のモデルの状態。Active、Legacy、End-of-Life の順に進み、終了日を過ぎると呼び出しが失敗する。
definition.en: The state of a model on Bedrock: Active, then Legacy, then End-of-Life, after which calls to it fail.

title.ja: ノートのアシスタント: デプロイ済みで呼ばれない月
title.en: Notes assistant: deployed, but never called for a month

ja: リクエストゼロ
テーブルは空で、保存量ゼロ
ガードレールは置いてあるだけでは課金されない（課金は text unit ごと）
ログは 1 週間で失効し、保存量ゼロ
en: No requests
The tables are empty; nothing is stored
A guardrail is not billed for existing (billing is per text unit)
Logs expire after a week; nothing is stored

title.ja: ノートのアシスタント: 月 1,000 問（Nova 2 Lite、jp. profile）
title.en: Notes assistant: 1,000 questions a month (Nova 2 Lite, jp. profile)

ja: 月 1,000 問。1 問あたりモデルを 3 回呼ぶと仮定（一覧、1 件読む、答える）
入力は 3 回の合計で 1 問あたり 4,000 token と仮定（会話は毎回すべて送り直す。実際の値はログの usage でわかる）
出力は 1 問あたり合計 200 token と仮定
prompt caching は使わない計算
ガードレールは sensitive information filter のみ。1 問あたり 6 text unit と仮定（3 回の呼び出しそれぞれで入力 1 と出力 1。複数回の呼び出しでの数え方は未確認）
Lambda は 256 MB、arm64、1 問あたり 8 秒と仮定
DynamoDB は 1 問あたり書き込み 2（予算の確保と精算）、読み込み 3 と仮定
1 問あたりログ 1 KB と仮定
データ転送は未算入
en: 1,000 questions a month, assuming three model calls each (list, read one, answer)
Assumed 4,000 input tokens per question over the three calls (the conversation is sent again every time; the real number is in the log's usage)
Assumed 200 output tokens per question in total
Calculated without prompt caching
The guardrail has the sensitive information filter only; assumed 6 text units per question (one in and one out for each of three calls; how units are counted across several calls is not confirmed)
Lambda at 256 MB on arm64, assumed 8 seconds per question
DynamoDB assumed at 2 writes (reserve and settle the budget) and 3 reads per question
Assumed 1 KB of logs per question
Data transfer is not included

items.basis: 1,000 questions x 4,000 input tokens, in 1K tokens
1,000 questions x 200 output tokens, in 1K tokens

title.ja: prompt caching の損得: 2,000 token の同じ先頭を 4 回送る会話を月 1,000 回、キャッシュなし（Nova 2 Lite）
title.en: Prompt caching arithmetic: 1,000 conversations a month that send the same 2,000-token prefix four times, no cache (Nova 2 Lite)

ja: 先頭の 2,000 token の分だけ。残りの入力と出力は含まない
4 回とも通常の入力として課金
en: The 2,000-token prefix only; the rest of the input and the output are not included
All four sends billed as ordinary input

title.ja: prompt caching の損得: 同じ会話、キャッシュあり（Nova 2 Lite）
title.en: Prompt caching arithmetic: the same conversations with a cache point (Nova 2 Lite)

ja: 1 回目が書き込み、2〜4 回目が読み出しになったと仮定（キャッシュに当たる保証はない）
各回が前の回から 5 分以内と仮定
en: Assumes the first send writes and the second to fourth read (a hit is never guaranteed)
Assumes each send comes within 5 minutes of the one before

title.ja: prompt caching の損得: 5,000 token の同じ先頭を 4 回送る会話を月 1,000 回、キャッシュなし（Claude Haiku 4.5）
title.en: Prompt caching arithmetic: 1,000 conversations a month that send the same 5,000-token prefix four times, no cache (Claude Haiku 4.5)

ja: 先頭の 5,000 token の分だけ（このモデルの下限は 4,096 token）
4 回とも通常の入力として課金
en: The 5,000-token prefix only (this model's minimum is 4,096 tokens)
All four sends billed as ordinary input

title.ja: prompt caching の損得: 同じ会話、キャッシュあり（Claude Haiku 4.5）
title.en: Prompt caching arithmetic: the same conversations with a cache point (Claude Haiku 4.5)

ja: 1 回目が書き込み（5 分の TTL）、2〜4 回目が読み出しになったと仮定（キャッシュに当たる保証はない）
en: Assumes the first send writes (5-minute TTL) and the second to fourth read (a hit is never guaranteed)

title.ja: 要約 10,000 件を on-demand で（Nova 2 Lite、推論の分だけ）
title.en: 10,000 summaries on demand (Nova 2 Lite, inference only)

en: Assumed 2,000 input and 150 output tokens each (chapter 17's assumption)

title.ja: 同じ 10,000 件を batch inference で（Nova 2 Lite、推論の分だけ）
title.en: The same 10,000 summaries as batch inference (Nova 2 Lite, inference only)

ja: token 数は on-demand と同じと仮定
S3 の保存とリクエストの料金は未算入
en: Token counts assumed equal to on demand
S3 storage and request charges are not included

note.ja: 110 件。手で書いた応答の列（ツールを使って答える、存在しないツール、JSON でない入力、ガードレールの停止、ツールの要求の途中での切断、答えの途中での切断、スロットリング、ツールを求め続ける、ノートの指示に従う）、不変条件を壊すテスト、構造化出力と 1 回の修正、予算の確保と精算、cache point の配置、batch の入出力、評価、アプリ、function URL のアダプター、CDK の assertion
note.en: 110 tests: hand-written answer sequences (answering with tools, a tool that does not exist, input that is not JSON, a guardrail block, a cut in the middle of a tool request, a cut in the middle of the answer, throttling, a model that never stops asking for tools, a model that obeys a note), the test that breaks the invariant, structured output with one repair, reserving and settling the budget, cache point placement, batch input and output, the evaluation, the app, the function URL adapter, and the CDK assertions

esbuild によるバンドル（Docker なし）を含む。9 リソース、8 種類
note.en: Includes the esbuild bundle (no Docker); 9 resources of 8 types

note.ja: 課金される。デプロイが前提

summary.ja: 36章は実際の Bedrock を一度も呼んでいない。実際の ConverseStream がツールの要求をこの章のスキーマとフィクスチャの形で返すこと、実際のモデルの振る舞い（ツールをいつ呼ぶか、断られたあと、ノートの指示、名指ししたツールの入力がスキーマに合うか）、評価の 4 ケースが通るかは未確認。Nova 2 Lite で toolChoice の名指しと cache checkpoint が通ること、Claude Haiku 4.5 で outputConfig.textFormat が jp. の profile 経由で通ること、キャッシュに当たること、Price List で USD 0 の cache write が請求でどう数えられるかも未確認。
summary.en: Chapter 36 has never called real Bedrock. Unconfirmed: that real ConverseStream returns tool requests in the shape of this chapter's schema and fixtures; how a real model behaves (when it calls a tool, what it does after a refusal, whether it obeys a note, whether a named tool's input fits the schema); whether the 4 evaluation cases pass. Also unconfirmed: that naming a tool in toolChoice and cache checkpoints work on Nova 2 Lite, that outputConfig.textFormat works on Claude Haiku 4.5 through the jp. profile, that the cache is hit, and how cache writes priced at USD 0 in the Price List are counted on a bill.

resume.ja: examples/36-bedrock/.env を用意して vp run bedrock:eval:live を実行する（課金される）。BEDROCK_MODEL_ID を替えて両方のモデルで回す。イベントの形が違えば src/converse.ts と fixtures/transcripts を直す。
resume.en: Prepare examples/36-bedrock/.env and run vp run bedrock:eval:live (billed), once per model by changing BEDROCK_MODEL_ID. If the event shapes differ, fix src/converse.ts and fixtures/transcripts.

summary.ja: 36章のスタックはデプロイしていない。cdkd が Cloud Control API 経由で AWS::Bedrock::Guardrail と GuardrailVersion を作成、更新、削除できること、sensitive information filters だけのガードレールが作れること、bedrock:ApplyGuardrail を自分のガードレールに絞ったロールでガードレール付きの ConverseStream が通ること、function URL のイベントの requestContext.authorizer.iam.userId が引き受けたロールでどういう値になるか、DynamoDB の条件付き更新が同時のリクエストで予算を守ること、出力の途中でガードレールが止めたときに届く断片、往復のある呼び出しでの text unit の数え方は未確認。
summary.en: The chapter 36 stack has not been deployed. Unconfirmed: that cdkd can create, update and delete AWS::Bedrock::Guardrail and GuardrailVersion through the Cloud Control API; that a guardrail with sensitive information filters only can be created; that ConverseStream with a guardrail passes with a role whose bedrock:ApplyGuardrail is narrowed to its own guardrail; what requestContext.authorizer.iam.userId holds in the function URL event for an assumed role; that the conditional update in DynamoDB holds the budget under simultaneous requests; which pieces arrive when a guardrail blocks partway through the output; how text units are counted in a call with several rounds.

resume.ja: vp run bedrock:infra:deploy、vp run bedrock:smoke、vp run bedrock:logs、vp run bedrock:infra:drift、vp run bedrock:infra:destroy の順に実行する。-c promptAttackFilter=standard を付けたデプロイも一度確かめる。
resume.en: Run vp run bedrock:infra:deploy, vp run bedrock:smoke, vp run bedrock:logs, vp run bedrock:infra:drift, and vp run bedrock:infra:destroy, in that order. Check a deploy with -c promptAttackFilter=standard once too.

summary.ja: batch inference のジョブは作っていない。入力ファイルの形と上限の検査は手元で確かめたが、S3 のバケット、サービスロール、CreateModelInvocationJob、出力の実際の形は未確認。structured outputs が batch で使えるかは、ドキュメントの 2 つのページ（batch-inference と structured-output）が食い違っている。
summary.en: No batch inference job was created. The input file's shape and the limit checks were verified locally, but the S3 buckets, the service role, CreateModelInvocationJob and the real shape of the output are unconfirmed. Whether structured outputs work in a batch is stated differently on two documentation pages (batch-inference and structured-output).

resume.ja: vp run bedrock:batch:plan の出力を S3 に置き、batch-iam-sr のとおりにサービスロールを作ってジョブを作成する。出力を src/batch.ts の parseOutputLine に通す。
resume.en: Put the output of vp run bedrock:batch:plan in S3, create the service role as batch-iam-sr describes, and create a job. Run the output through parseOutputLine in src/batch.ts.

summary.ja: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore と Agents Classic は動かしていない。本文はドキュメントに書かれた構成の紹介だけ。
summary.en: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Agents Classic were not run. The chapter only presents the structure described in their documentation.

resume.ja: AgentCore の Harness か Runtime で同じツールを動かし、呼び出した人の ID がツールまでどう届くかを確かめる。
resume.en: Run the same tools on AgentCore Harness or Runtime and check how the caller's identity reaches the tools.
